scope: Proposition 15.2 (A quantitative additive Gram bound) of the manuscript “The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$” (preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 003 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8fe93046f8cf5ef1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 104. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the arithmetic data S, T, b∗, ξ, the annular weight W1, and a ray class σ ∈ T. Let Q, Y ′ ≥ 1 be in fixed polynomial ranges in Z, and suppose Pa = Y ′2 /Q ≥ 1. For a real height ν, put Am = Am,σ,ν(Y ′) as defined in Section 6. For every fixed row ball qm ≪ Q and every ϵ > 0, one has X qm≪Q |Am|2 ≪ (1 + |ν|)JGr Q Y ′  1 + P1/6 a + P2 a Y ′  Zϵ . (15.4) Here JGr is a fixed seminorm order, independent of the moving scales and of ν. The same assertion holds for any fixed finite linear combination of the ray coefficients 1s∈σχs(b∗)/ξ(s). No arbitrary row-dependent arithmetic coefficient is asserted.
